title: Accessibility (VoiceOver, Dynamic Type)
summary: Accessibility means everyone can use your app: blind users with VoiceOver, people who need larger text (Dynamic Type), reduced motion, sufficient contrast. It is also a legal and App Store quality expectation.
body: **In simple words:** VoiceOver reads the screen aloud and users navigate by swiping. Each element needs a good **label** (what it is), **value** (current state), **hint** (what happens) and **traits** (button, header, selected).

**VoiceOver basics:** standard controls are accessible by default. Custom views need `isAccessibilityElement = true` and labels. Icon-only buttons must have a label ("Delete", not "trash.fill"). Group related elements (a cell with title, price, rating) into one element with a combined label. Hide decorative images.

**Dynamic Type:** use text styles (`.body`, `.headline`, `UIFont.preferredFont(forTextStyle:)`) so text grows with the user's setting. Layout must adapt: allow multi-line labels, switch horizontal layouts to vertical at accessibility sizes, use scroll views.

**Other settings:** Reduce Motion (tone down animations), Reduce Transparency, Increase Contrast, Bold Text, Smart Invert. Colour contrast at least 4.5:1 for text; never use colour alone to convey meaning. Tap targets at least 44×44 pt.
**Testing:** Accessibility Inspector (audit), turn VoiceOver on and use the app, Xcode Previews with large Dynamic Type, automated `XCUIApplication().performAccessibilityAudit()` in UI tests.
**Staff angle:** build accessibility into design-system components so every feature gets it for free, add audits to CI, and include it in the definition of done.
keyPoints: VoiceOver needs labels, values, hints and traits; group related content.
Dynamic Type via text styles; layouts must adapt to large sizes.
Respect Reduce Motion and contrast settings; 44×44 pt tap targets.
Test with Accessibility Inspector, real VoiceOver, and automated audits.
Solve it once in the design system.

mistakes: Fixed font sizes and fixed-height containers that clip large text.
Treating accessibility as a final QA step.
followups: **How do you make a custom slider accessible?** Mark it as an element with `.adjustable` trait and implement `accessibilityIncrement/Decrement` (SwiftUI: `accessibilityAdjustableAction`).
**What is the accessibility rotor?** A VoiceOver feature to jump between headings, links, etc. Mark section titles with the header trait.
